record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.original_question: For continuous maps f:S^1→S^1 and I_δ(f)=∫∫_{S^1×S^1}1_{\{|f(x)-f(y)|≥δ\}}/|x-y|^2\,dx\,dy, does there exist a universal constant c such that |deg f|≤c·δ·I_δ(f) for every 0<δ≤√3?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.3 ([17, Open Problem 3]). Does there exist a (universal) constant c such that (5.5) |deg f| ≤ c δ Iδ(f) for all f ∈ C(S1; S1) and all δ ≤ √3?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle, and for a continuous map $f:S^1\to S^1$ let $\deg f\in\mathbb{Z}$ denote its topological degree. For $\delta>0$ define
$$I_\delta(f)=\iint_{S^1\times S^1}\frac{\mathbf{1}_{\{|f(x)-f(y)|\ge \delta\}}}{|x-y|^2}\,dx\,dy,$$
where $|x-y|$ denotes the Euclidean distance between $x,y\in S^1\subset\mathbb{R}^2$.

Does there exist a universal constant $c>0$ such that
$$|\deg f|\le c\,\delta\, I_\delta(f)$$
holds for every continuous map $f:S^1\to S^1$ and every $\delta$ with $0<\delta\le\sqrt{3}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in Brezis's collection of favorite open problems, originating from earlier work of Bourgain–Brezis–Nguyen on new estimates for the topological degree. Web search did not surface a resolution; recent surveys on degree estimates still cite it as open.
